sample.title: The World's Most Aggressive EV Push Isn't in China | Bloomberg Primer
sample.description:
(Corrects the spelling of Mia Mottley at 06:01) In 2024, Ethiopia became the first country to ban imports of new gasoline-powered cars, and the main reason wasn't global warming. Ethiopia was spending billions of dollars every year on imported fuel it couldn’t afford, and subsequently defaulted on its debt. Cheap hydropower from Africa’s largest dam made electric vehicles a practical alternative, and Chinese-made EVs — some assembled locally — quickly filled dealership lots. Today, Ethiopia’s EV share outpaces the global average. But sticker prices are too high for most, the grid remains patchy and armed conflict is flaring in the country and across the region. Can Ethiopia make its unprecedented bet on EVs pay off?

sample.title: Inside Mexico City’s Housing Theft Crisis
sample.description:
In Mexico City, housing theft happens on average 11 times a day, often when homeowners are on vacation or have died, leaving properties vacant. In many cases criminal gangs move in, claiming ownership in an effort to profit from a gentrification wave that’s boosted home prices.

Many such “dispossessions” can involve title fraud and even complicit public officials. Mexico City recorded 2,676 cases this year through August, according to public records, bringing the total over the past decade to nearly 41,000. 

The sheer number of incidents lays bare two key problems for President Claudia Sheinbaum: security and the cost of living. While homicides have plunged under her watch, reports of extortion are at their highest in more than a decade. She also has made expanding access to affordable homes a national priority, yet nowhere is the challenge more stark than the capital, where protests frequently break out over evictions and rising foreign demand.

sample.description:

France now pays more to borrow than former crisis hot spots like Greece and Italy. With government debt growing faster than the economy, the pressure on France to rein in its budget deficit has never been higher. CNBC's Liz Napolitano reports.

sample.title: How the Democrats’ historic night of wins unfolded | BBC News
sample.description:
The Democrats have won a blowout victory in the US midterm elections, winning the Senate and the House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.
 
In the Senate race, Republican strongholds have been toppled by the Democrats in Texas, Ohio and Kansas, which last elected a Democrat almost 100 years ago.
 
Trump has congratulated the Democrats on a “good job” and acknowledged that gas prices hurt Republicans during the midterm races, saying people "didn't like it" when they had to pay more for fuel.
 
The midterm elections happen mid-way through every 4-year presidential election cycle, giving Americans the chance to elect members of Congress, which is made up of the House of Representatives and the Senate.
 
Here is how the night unfolded.
